mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when this trigger is met (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which is associated with lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases uncertainty and volatility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such dual-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) over the past six months indicates a rebalancing toward consumption, which supports corporate earnings and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero when this correlation is observed.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during these episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals reduced household buffer and impending consumption drawdown, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when this trigger is met.
